Article Title: TMC MP Nadimul Haque under ED scanner; 7 locations raided in money laundering case
Article Text:
The case involves 'allegations concerning publication and dissemination of material promoting communal disharmony and also contains allegations regarding illegal transactions, unaccounted cash transactions and funding from suspicious sources.'

NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Monday conducted searches at the residence of Trinamool Congress Rajya Sabha MP Nadimul Haque and six other premises across Delhi, West Bengal and Jharkhand. The move comes as part of a money laundering investigation linked to Urdu newspaper Akhbar-E-Mashriq.The searches, which began early Monday, were carried out by the ED's Kolkata zonal office in Kolkata, Delhi and Ranchi in connection with a case against Akhbar-E-Mashriq Pvt Ltd and its director Mohd Nadimul Haque. The operation was conducted in coordination with security forces and the state police forces concerned.According to officials, the Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) was registered after an FIR was filed by the Bidhannagar Police Commissionerate in West Bengal.The case involves "allegations concerning publication and dissemination of material promoting communal disharmony and also contains allegations regarding illegal transactions, unaccounted cash transactions and funding from suspicious sources."The agency is examining the financial dealings of the newspaper, Haque and other entities and individuals named in the case to trace the alleged proceeds of crime and establish the money trail.During the searches, ED teams are collecting documentary and digital evidence as part of the investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA).The searches were still underway at the premises on Monday, with further details on any evidence recovered and the agency's next course of action awaited.The action forms part of the ED's broader investigations into cases where alleged proceeds of crime are suspected to have been generated or routed through financial transactions involving individuals or entities under investigation.
Article Summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) conducted searches at the residence of Trinamool Congress Rajya Sabha MP Nadimul Haque. The move comes as part of a money laundering investigation linked to Urdu newspaper Akhbar-E-Mashriq. The action forms part of the ED's broader investigations into cases where alleged proceeds of crime are suspected.

Article Title: Politicians who hit doctors should be taken into custody, not allowed to roam free: SC
Article Text:
Govt in a bind over SC ruling on ‘creamy layer’

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Monday expressed concern over growing incidents of doctors being beaten by the members of political parties in Maharashtra and directed the government to take such politicians immediately into custody.The apex court's observation came a day after Shiv Sena office-bearers allegedly assaulted doctors and other staff at a healthcare facility in Maharashtra's Palghar district.The incident reportedly took place early on Sunday after a commotion erupted in the corridors of Relief Hospital over the discharge of a person who was injured during the Dahi Handi festival.Palghar Police have registered a case against at least 17 people, including members of the Eknath Shinde-led faction.According to CCTV footage, one of them also slapped a receptionist and threatened a woman employee when they tried to intervene.According to the complaint lodged by a hospital employee, Shiv Sena district chief Kundan Sankhe, city chief Rahul Gharat and others had entered the hospital's emergency department and got into an argument with doctors. A receptionist who tried to intervene was seen being slapped in the CCTV footage.Some of the party members even barged into the hospital's Intensive Care Unit (ICU).In a similar case, a Shiv Sena corporator was accused of assaulting doctors at a civic hospital in Kalyan. A case was registered against the accused, Ramesh Mhatre.
Article Summary: Supreme Court expresses concern over growing incidents of doctors being beaten by political parties in Maharashtra. Court orders government to take such politicians immediately into custody. Shiv Sena office-bearers allegedly assaulted doctors and other staff at a healthcare facility in Maharashtra's Palghar district.

Article Title: After meeting Bihar youth, Rahul slams PM Modi, Samrat Choudhary
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi meets Bihar youth, hits out at PM Modi, CM Samrat

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi Sunday lashed out at PM Narendra Modi and Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary over the police action against protesting students in the state, asking while their broken bones would be fixed, if their shattered dreams could be restored.Gandhi shared a video of his recent meeting with students and youngsters from Bihar who, he said, endured "horrific police brutality" for raising their voices against alleged irregularities in the examination system.In his post accompanying the video, Rahul said, "Imagine, what sin had these children committed that they were shot with bullets? Article Title: BJP to launch month-long ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’ nationwide to mark 25 years of PM Modi’s parliamentary political journey
Article Text:
BJP to launch month-long ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’ nationwide to mark 25 years of PM Modi’s parliamentary political journey

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Along with the rest of the country, Assam is gearing up to observe the “Seva Sankalp Abhiyan” from September 17 to October 17, commemorating the completion of 25 years of dedicated public service and political commitment by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in parliamentary politics.According to the release, Prime Minister Narendra Modi first took oath as the Chief Minister of Gujarat on October 7, 2001. Subsequently, the widely acclaimed and dynamic leader assumed office as the Prime Minister of India for the first time on May 26, 2014.Having secured the mandate of the people for three consecutive terms, he continues to serve as the Prime Minister, backed by the unwavering support and confidence of the people of the country.To mark the completion of 25 years of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s journey in public and parliamentary life, a vibrant calendar of 13 programmes has been prepared for nationwide observance from his birthday on September 17 to October 17.According to BJP Assam Pradesh spokesperson Pranjal Kalita, extensive preparations are already underway for the implementation of programmes centred around initiatives such as “Namo Seva Gatha,” “Anganwadi Utsav,” “Rangoli,” “Parivartan Ki Kahani,” “Seva Setu Abhiyan,” “Seva Ke Nimitta Bhagidari,” “Jan Sevak Mahakumbh,” “Painting, Elocution and Quiz Competitions,” “Viksit Bharat Sankalp Yatra,” “Seva Jyoti Yatra,” and the “National Innovation Competition,” among others.A state-level committee has already been constituted to oversee and monitor preparations for the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan. The committee is headed by State General Secretary Anup Barman and comprises Cabinet Minister Dr Ranoj Pegu, Guwahati Lok Sabha MP Bijuli Kalita Medhi, Rajya Sabha MP Terash Gowala, State Secretary Ratul Sharma, MLA Bijoy Malakar and Yuva Morcha president Rakesh Das.In addition, several sub-committees have been constituted, with senior party leaders entrusted with responsibilities at the state, regional and district levels for the effective and coordinated implementation of the programmes being organised under the nationwide campaign.The inaugural programme of the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, titled “Ashirbadar Banti” (Lamp of Blessings), will be held on September 17, coinciding with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday.BJP Assam Pradesh spokesperson Pranjal Kalita said party workers across more than 31,000 booths in Assam will light lamps at their respective homes as a gesture of blessings and goodwill for the Prime Minister.Kalita further stated that district-level training programmes for the smooth and systematic execution of the various activities under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan have commenced on Sunday.He added that Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma and State BJP president and MP Dilip Saikia will oversee the implementation of all programmes.Ministers of the state government, legislators belonging to the ruling party and BJP karyakartas across the state are also expected to participate actively in the month-long campaign. (ANI)
Article Summary: BJP to launch month-long ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’ nationwide to mark 25 years of PM Modi’s parliamentary political journey. To mark the completion of 25 years, a vibrant calendar of 13 programmes has been prepared for nationwide observance.

Article Title: 'Bones will mend but shattered dreams?' Rahul Gandhi meets Bihar students shot at during protest
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi with injured student protesters

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday shared a video of his interaction with three students who were injured during police action amid recent student protests in Bihar.The three were part of a group of students from Bihar who met the Lok Sabha leader of opposition at his Delhi residence on September 3. In a social media post, Gandhi said the three students had been “shot at”, referring to a protest in Siwan, Bihar, on July 25.“Think about it: what crime had these children committed that they were shot? They had asked the government for just three things — education, employment, and accountability,” the Raebareli MP wrote on X.The leg bone of one of the students, he added, was shattered after he was hit by a bullet fired from an AK-47.“Along with it, his dream of joining the Army and serving the country was shattered too. Bullets tore through the shoulders of two other students,” Rahul Gandhi wrote.“They were not criminals. They were children from poor families who had gone out to study carrying the dreams of their families — some wanted a good job, while others wanted to change the circumstances of their homes,” he added.The Congress leader further remarked that while their physical wounds would heal, there is no answer to how the psychological trauma they had suffered could be treated."Mr prime minister, Mr chief minister — their broken bones will heal. Can you give them back their broken dreams?" Rahul Gandhi said, questioning Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary.Several parts of Bihar witnessed student protests, some of which turned violent, on July 25 as part of a broader agitation by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in Delhi. The CJP was leading protests demanding the resignation of then-Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET paper leak issue, along with reforms in the education system.The CJP, which had been protesting at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar since June 21, called off its agitation on July 25, shortly after Pradhan resigned. Union minister Pralhad Joshi has since been given additional charge of the Education ministry.The Bihar government has told the Supreme Court that a police constable fired four rounds from an AK-47 into the air after being trapped in a crowd, while maintaining that no protester was injured in the firing. The constable has since been suspended.
Article Summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi shared a video of his interaction with three students injured during police action amid recent student protests in Bihar. The three were part of a group of students from Bihar who met the Lok Sabha leader of opposition at his Delhi residence on September 3. In a social media post, Gandhi said the three students had been "shot at"

Article Title: MCOCA action against two accused from ‘Gold Hunters Gang’ in Kolhapur
Article Text:
Kolhapur

:





Special inspector general of police, Ranjan Kumar Sharma, has approved action under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) against two alleged members of the “Gold Hunters Gang,” arrested in a gold chain theft case in Kolhapur.The accused are alleged gang leader, Vaibhav Narayan Adole (26), a Hinjewadi resident and native of Yerla in Amravati district, and Karan Gorakh Jagadhane (19), a resident of Vidhate Vasti in Aundh and native of Pimpalwadi in Paithan.Police said 28 serious cases, including forcible theft, housebreaking and vehicle theft, were registered against the duo across Maharashtra, including six in Kolhapur.They allegedly engaged an elderly woman in conversation before fleeing, on the pretext of asking for an address before snatching a 20gm mangalsutra from her neck, near Ambai Tank in Kolhapur.A parallel investigation by the local crime branch led to their arrest at Shirwal in Satara district. Police said 26 cases involving gold chains stolen from elderly women were registered across Maharashtra.The investigation found that the duo had allegedly committed offences in Kolhapur, Sangli, Satara, Sawantwadi, Kankavli, Kudal, Pune, Wardha, Buldhana, Beed, Akola, Amravati and Yavatmal.Superintendent of police, Nilotpal directed Juna Rajwada police station inspector, Kiran Londhe to prepare the MCOCA proposal. Havaldar Ranjit Desai and colleagues prepared it.Additional superintendent of police Annasaheb Jadhav, deputy superintendent Priya Patil, local crime branch inspector Sushant Chavan and assistant faujdar Sachin Patil scrutinised the proposal before sending it for approval.
Article Summary: Alleged gang leader Vaibhav Narayan Adole (26) and Karan Gorakh Jagadhane (19) arrested in Kolhapur. Police said 28 serious cases, including forcible theft, housebreaking and vehicle theft, were registered against the duo across Maharashtra.

Article Title: 'Grabbed hand and attempted to disrobe': Cab driver tries to assault woman passenger near Navi Mumbai airport
Article Text:
Police have registered a case and are searching for the accused driver (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver who took the vehicle to a deserted road near Navi Mumbai airport late on Saturday night, police said on Sunday.The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport, police said. The accused allegedly stopped the cab on the pretext of drinking water before moving to the rear seat beside the woman, police said.According to the police, the woman was travelling to Panvel after a friend booked a cab for her following the party."The driver stopped the vehicle on the deserted service road, stepped out briefly, and then re-entered the car, sitting on the rear seat next to the woman. He allegedly grabbed her hand and attempted to disrobe her," said an official of the Navi Mumbai Police.The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.After the incident, the woman contacted her family and went to Panvel Police Station to lodge a complaint.Since the alleged incident took place within the jurisdiction of Navi Mumbai airport police station, Panvel police escorted her to the appropriate police station.Based on her complaint, Navi Mumbai Airport Police registered a case against the accused, identified as Mohammad Afzal Shaikh, under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Police have launched a search for Shaikh and are using technical intelligence to trace his whereabouts.Further investigation is underway.(With ANI inputs)(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)
Article Summary: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver. The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport. The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.

Article Title: FIR lodged after 3,400 SIR forms found in Navi Mumbai shop; 5 BLOs suspended
Article Text:
An FIR was registered against Suraj Patil for illegally possessing voter enumeration forms





NAVI MUMBAI: The police have registered an FIR against Suraj Patil, a nodal BJP youth wing committee member, for illegally possessing and converting special intensive revision (SIR) voter enumeration forms for “personal use” and for breaking the maintenance of secrecy of voting under Section 314 of the BNS and Section 128 of the Representation of People Act.Section 314 of the BNS deals with dishonestly converting a movable property for own use, for which the punishment is at least two years imprisonment.The matter came to light on Thursday, after an advocate working for the Shiv Sena (UBT) noticed hundreds of original SIR forms lying at a photocopier’s shop in Kharghar. He alerted the police.The accused (Patil) had decamped from the Kharghar police station, leading to high drama throughout the night.Authorities seized 3,404 SIR forms, including 11 blank ones, of 11 polling stations from the photocopier’s shop next to the Ramsheth Thakur Public School in Sector 19, Kharghar, by Shiv Sena (UBT) nodal chief Balesh Bhojane.Five booth-level officers (BLOs) served with show-cause notices were suspended by the Panvel City Municipal Corporation (PCMC) chief Mangesh Chitale.They include three data entry operators working as booth-level officers from a private company, Saunik Integrated & Security Pvt Ltd, Bhayandar, engaged by the PCMC.Their names are Sulochana Mane, Prashant Mhatre and Rahul Bhagat.The Shiv Sena (UBT) had earlier warned the Panvel sub-divisional officer through a letter about various lapses in the electoral process.A two-member inquiry committee comprising a Panvel deputy municipal commissioner, Nanasaheb Kamathe, and an assistant electoral registration officer, has been formed to conduct a comprehensive probe.Bhojane said, “MLAs Jitendra Awhad and Rohit Pawar have tweeted the video regarding the original SIR forms at the Kharghar shop. We demand action against the Panvel SDO as he did not take preventive measures despite our complaint about forms filed at the BJP offices. The FIR was filed only after more than hundreds of our workers assembled at the police station.”After learning about the incident, Raigad district communication head of Shiv Sena (UBT) Prasad Bhoir lodged a complaint with the electoral registration officer.“Yesterday evening, the election registration office (ERO) received information that a person is xeroxing enumeration forms at a Xerox centre at Kharghar sector 19. Immediately, the assistant election registration officer visited the site and found that one Suraj Patil was holding around 3,400 enumeration forms and xeroxing it illegally,” Raigad district collector Kishan Javale said.
Article Summary: Police have registered an FIR against Suraj Patil, a nodal BJP youth wing committee member, for illegally possessing and converting voter enumeration forms. The matter came to light on Thursday, after an advocate working for the Shiv Sena (UBT) noticed hundreds of original SIR forms lying at a photocopier’s shop in Kharghar.

Article Title: 'Minor injuries, kept in ICU': Govinda group file FIR against Palghar doctor, threaten sit-in outside police station
Article Text:
Sena’s district chief Kundan Sankhe claimed they went to Relief Hospital after receiving complaints that the govindas were not being allowed to leave





PALGHAR: A fresh twist has emerged in the alleged assault of a receptionist at Relief Hospital in Palghar, with the injured Govinda participants whose treatment triggered the dispute filing a written complaint against the doctor at Palghar police station.A case has already been registered against 17 people, including Shiv Sena district chief Kundan Sankhe, in connection with the alleged assault.In their complaint, the Govinda participants alleged that although they had suffered only minor injuries, they were deliberately kept in the ICU and were not discharged despite repeatedly requesting the doctor to release them.They further alleged that the doctor ignored their requests, following which they sought the intervention of Sankhe. The participants claimed that unnecessary treatment was continued despite there being no medical requirement for it.The complainants have demanded that a case be registered against the doctor over the alleged conduct.Palghar MLA Rajendra Gavit, along with senior Shiv Sena functionaries, party workers and members of the Govinda group, gathered outside Palghar police station in support of the complaint.Gavit warned that the group would stage a sit-in outside the police station until a case was registered against the doctor.The latest complaint comes amid the ongoing controversy over the alleged assault of the hospital receptionist and the case registered against Sankhe and others.
Article Summary: Govinda participants claim they were deliberately kept in the ICU and were not discharged despite repeatedly requesting the doctor to release them. A case has already been registered against 17 people, including Shiv Sena district chief Kundan Sankhe, in connection with the alleged assault.

Article Title: MPSC aspirants to protest in Pune on Monday; support pours in from CJP, Rahul Gandhi, Aaditya Thackeray
Article Text:
Rohit Pawar announces the MPSC students’ protest march

Pune:





A day before a protest march announced by Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) aspirants against alleged irregularities in the recruitment process, demanding either resignation or removal of the commission’s chairperson, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) as well as opposition leaders like LOP Rahul Gandhi of Congress and MLA Aaditya Thackeray of Shiv Sena (UBT) extended their support to the agitation.In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi said thousands of students across Maharashtra were protesting peacefully, with their concerns extending beyond a particular examination or recruitment process to a broader loss of faith in the system. “Whether at Centre or in the state, every student is fed up with BJP govt. Paper leaks, stalled recruitments, unaffordable education, inhumane hostel conditions, poisonous food and fraud in DBT. And now, by taking control of a constitutional body like MPSC, it has destroyed the institution’s credibility,” he said.The Congress leader said that every demand from students for their successful future is justified. He said govt must listen to their voice and act immediately, else this echo of students will only grow louder until justice is served.The scheduled protest of MPSC students that will start from Omkareshwar Temple and culminate at the Pune district collector’s office also received backing from CJP chief Abhijit Dipke, who announced that CJP supports the demands.Some office-bearers of CJP also met agitating students to declare that they too will take part in the march.Thackeray, who was in Pune on Sunday to participate in the protest march by Hinjewadi residents and IT professionals for better infrastructure, also met MPSC aspirants later in the day and announced his party’s support for them. “We stand with MPSC students. The local Shiv Sena (UBT) and Yuva Sena will participate in Monday’s march,” he said.NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar met MPSC aspirants on Saturday and addressed a press-conference alongside them to announce the proposed protest march. Pawar has also been raising concerns over the FDA inspector recruitment examination, which came under scrutiny following allegations of a question paper leak. Police have arrested several people in connection with the case and the exam was cancelled in Aug after leak was confirmed.The developments come after state govt formed a committee on Sept 4 to review the existing recruitment examination system and recommend measures to make it more transparent and reliable.Meanwhile, BJP MLA Vikram Pachpute, who met MPSC aspirants in Pune on Sunday, said efforts were being made to resolve the issue through dialogue and to persuade the protesting students. He said the agitation should not be exploited for political gains. On the demand for the removal of MPSC chairperson Vivek Bhimanwar, Pachpute said the commission is an autonomous body and its chairperson is appointed by the governor. “Govt does not even have the authority to demand his resignation,” he said.
Article Summary: MPSC aspirants are protesting against alleged irregularities in the recruitment process. They are demanding either resignation or removal of the commission’s chairperson. Opposition leaders like LOP Rahul Gandhi of Congress and MLA Aaditya Thackeray of Shiv Sena (UBT) extended their support to the agitation.

Article Title: Firing mastermind on run, probe to be shifted to crime branch
Article Text: Nagpur: Investigation into the firing on Congress corporator Subham Motghare’s residence at Shravan Nagar is set to be shifted to Crime Branch, with the mastermind and a mysterious woman linked to the case still on the run.So far, seven accused have been arrested, including the shooter identified as Ankush Tomaskar and the bike rider Rushabh Nagdeve. The case was cracked with a clue picked up by naik constable Roshan Tiwari, Nitin Verma and PSI Nitin Chulpar. Police suspect the attack may have been a supari (contract crime).The case was registered at Wathoda police station. Police stations lack dedicated manpower needed for a focused probe in such cases. Sources said commissioner of police Vishwas Nangre Patil has decided to hand over the probe to Crime Branch, which will follow structured and more focused investigation methods to unearth a deep-rooted criminal angle.Investigators plan to nab another four to five persons and are likely to invoke the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA), given the organised nature of the crime.Crime Branch will also work to establish the exact motive behind the attack and identify those who allegedly hired the shooters. Crime Branch will prioritise tracking down the alleged mastermind and the mysterious woman, said sources.
Article Summary: The case was cracked with a clue picked up by naik constable Roshan Tiwari, Nitin Verma and PSI Nitin Chulpar. Police suspect the attack may have been a supari (contract crime) Crime Branch will prioritise tracking down the alleged mastermind and the mysterious woman.

Article Title: Enforce SC’s 10pm curb on DJ across state, don’t act selectively: Sule
Article Text:
Nagpur:





NCP (SP) Lok Sabha member Supriya Sule on Sunday said the state govt should implement Supreme Court ’s 10pm cut-off for DJs uniformly across Maharashtra instead of imposing an outright ban in some cities and looking away elsewhere.On the controversy over playing DJs and loudspeakers at processions, Sule said, “The matter has escalated. I would urge the govt to develop a consensus as there are big festivals like Ganeshotsav, Navratri and then Diwali. We need to sensibly bring all sections of society together and find a way forward,” she said.Supporters of DJ have claimed students themselves are dancing in processions, “hence using them as a shield to impose a ban isn’t justified”. Sule drew a distinction. “There is no objection to dancing or to what anyone wants to do. The objection is about implementation. What does the Supreme Court’s order say? There is an order on decibel limit and that DJs must be shut off after 10pm,” she said.Citing the example of Nagpur, where police claimed to have ensured that noise limits while playing DJ were not breached, Sule said that instead of a ban, options that could fit within rules should be explored.“If rules for DJ can work in Nagpur, why can’t the chief minister get this implemented across Maharashtra by personally overseeing it? This is not for any individual, it is for children, for hospitals, for senior citizens,” she said.On reports of violence against supporters of a DJ ban, Sule said her party will never accept raising hand against someone. “Culture must continue, but it has to run by rule of law, not by anyone’s whims. We are not the ones who would resort to violence,” she said.
Article Summary: Supriya Sule said the state govt should implement Supreme Court’s 10pm cut-off for DJs uniformly across Maharashtra. “There is no objection to dancing or to what anyone wants to do. The objection is about implementation,” she said.

Article Title: Man gets 7-year rigorous imprisonment for sexually harassing minor girl in Nashik’s Panchavati
Article Text:
Nashik

:





A special Pocso court in Nashik on Friday sentenced a 44-year-old man to seven years of rigorous imprisonment for sexually harassing a minor girl after luring her with snacks in the Panchavati area in 2020.District and sessions judge R N Pandhare convicted the accused under Section 10 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act, 2012. The court also imposed a fine of Rs 3,000, with an additional three months of simple imprisonment in case of default.The court further directed the convict to pay Rs 50,000 as compensation to the girl within a month. Failure to do so will attract an additional one-year simple imprisonment.According to the prosecution, the incident occurred on Nov 9, 2020, between 4pm and 5pm at a slum locality in Panchavati. The accused allegedly took advantage of the absence of the girl’s family members, lured the girl with biscuits and sexually harassed her. He was also accused of engaging in obscene behaviour.Based on a complaint lodged by the girl’s family, Panchavati police registered an offence under sections 354 and 354(A) of the Indian Penal Code, along with relevant provisions of the Pocso Act.The investigation was conducted by then sub-inspector Dhanashree Patil of Panchavati police station. She collected crucial circumstantial evidence and subsequently filed a chargesheet before the court.Additional public prosecutors Bhanupriya Pethkar and R P Gavit represented the state and presented witness testimonies and evidence before the court, leading to the conviction. Following the verdict, Nashik police commissioner Sandeep Karnik and deputy commissioner of police (crime) Kirankumar Chavan lauded the efforts of the investigating officers, prosecution team and court liaison staff for securing the conviction.
Article Summary: A special Pocso court in Nashik on Friday sentenced a 44-year-old man to seven years of rigorous imprisonment for sexually harassing a minor girl. The court also imposed a fine of Rs 3,000, with an additional three months of simple imprisonment in case of default. The incident occurred on Nov 9, 2020, between 4pm and 5pm at a slum locality in Panchavati.

Article Title: Tribal woman dies after family planning surgery in Salem; relatives lay siege to collectorate in protest
Article Text:
Over 100 relatives and villagers laid siege to Salem district collectorate in protest

Salem:





A tribal woman died at the Attur govt Hospital on Thursday, after her health deteriorated following a sterilisation surgery at Pethanaickenpalayam primary health centre in Salem district.The deceased has been identified as M Sumathi, 23, of Soolankurichi hill village in Karumanthurai. She was referred to Attur govt hospital soon after the sterilisation procedure but died without responding to treatment. She had delivered her third child about 45 days ago.Over 100 relatives and villagers including her husband Matheawaran, 30, laid siege to Salem district collectorate in protest. They alleged that a botched surgery had caused her death and demanded justice.Police held talks with the protesters and officials assured them that a proper inquiry would be held against the doctors concerned and appropriate action taken. The protesters subsequently withdrew their protest.Attur rural police have registered a case and are investigating.
Article Summary: The deceased has been identified as M Sumathi, 23, of Soolankurichi hill village in Karumanthurai. She was referred to Attur govt hospital soon after the sterilisation procedure but died without responding to treatment.

Article Title: Not an act of political vendetta: Nirmal Kumar
Article Text:
Electricity minister C T R Nirmal Kumar on Saturday said the searches conducted by directorate of vigilance and anti-corruption (DVAC) at properties linked to former minister K N Nehru were not an act of political vendetta.





Madurai: Electricity minister C T R Nirmal Kumar on Saturday said the searches conducted by directorate of vigilance and anti-corruption (DVAC) at properties linked to former minister K N Nehru were not an act of political vendetta.Speaking to reporters in Madurai, he said no one had the authority to interfere with the DVAC’s functioning. “The searches were routine and based on the evidence. No one can interfere with the DVAC. No one knows what is happening there. The department will release details,” he said, rejecting allegations that the TVK govt’s action was politically motivated.Asked about statements by AIADMK and DMK leaders that the TVK govt would not last, Nirmal Kumar said they indicated that the two parties were together. He also said there was a possibility of the AIADMK, DMK and BJP forming an alliance for the next election.Regarding the omission of the Board of Trustees’ names from the invitation for the consecration ceremony of Sri Meenakshi Sundareswarar temple, Nirmal Kumar said, “None of us will interfere in temple affairs, particularly those concerning the HR&CE department. Even our review is limited to assessing the arrangements made for devotees. We will not repeat the mistake made by the previous govt in temple matters.”
Article Summary: Electricity minister C T R Nirmal Kumar said the searches conducted by directorate of vigilance and anti-corruption (DVAC) at properties linked to former minister K N Nehru were not an act of political vendetta. “The searches were routine and based on the evidence. No one can interfere with the DVAC,” he said.

Article Title: Salem corporation council meeting disrupted over mayor’s demand for removal of deputy mayor chair from dais
Article Text: COIMBATORE: Tension flared at the Salem corporation council meeting on Friday when mayor A Ramachandran, who belongs to DMK, refused to conduct the proceedings, insisting that the chair of deputy mayor Saradha Devi, who belongs to Congress, be moved from the dais.The council meeting of Salem corporation, scheduled to begin at 11am, started 20 minutes late after the mayor entered the hall. Instead of taking his designated seat, the mayor sat among the councillors and declared that he would not preside over the session. He stated that during the previous council meeting, he had ordered to remove the deputy mayor’s seat from near the mayor’s chair. However, he alleged that the Salem corporation commissioner overruled his directive and insisted on retaining deputy mayor’s chair next to that of the mayor. “I will not conduct this meeting where I am not given the authority,” Ramachandran said.DMK councillors protested demanding the removal of the deputy mayor’s chair from the dais. When corporation staffers attempted to remove the chair, Saradha Devi launched a sit-in protest in the council hall. She accused the mayor of showing gender bias and disrespect.She said, “The mayor does not give me the respect I deserve because I am a woman.My chair has been right next to the mayor’s for the last four years; why should it be removed now? I respect this council, and I will not allow my seat to be moved.”Following the uproar, a closed-door reconciliation meeting was convened between the corporation commissioner, mayor, deputy mayor, and DMK councillors. Emerging from the discussions, Saradha Devi alleged, “They spoke about shifting my seat from the dais and asked whether I wanted the ‘chair’ or a ‘share.’ I made it clear that I only want my chair.”The deadlock remained unresolved. Upon returning to the council hall, mayor Ramachandran announced that all resolutions were postponed due to the disruption. He left the hall after that. However, Saradha Devi continued her protest.Tension between Congress and DMK councillors started after the national party left the DMK alliance to join the TVK govt in the state in May.
Article Summary: DMK councillors protested demanding the removal of the deputy mayor’s chair from the dais. When corporation staffers attempted to remove the chair, Saradha Devi launched a sit-in protest in the council hall. She accused the mayor of showing gender bias and disrespect.

Article Title: Police intercepts car in Angamaly, seize 12kg ganja
Article Text:
Kochi:





Ernakulam Rural police seized 12kg of cannabis from a car near Angamaly on Saturday.Charles Dennis, 29, and Praveen Das, 28, of Punnapra, Alappuzha, were arrested by a joint team of rural Dansaf unit and Angamaly Police.Acting on intelligence received by district police chief K S Sudarshan, officers intercepted the accused near Angamaly TB Junction. The ganja was found carefully packed in bags concealed in the car’s boot. Investigators say the consignment was headed for Alappuzha. The investigation team included narcotic cell DSP C Binu Kumar, Aluva DSP Baiju Paulose, and Angamaly SHO PM Razik.Earlier this week, on Tuesday, Kochi city police conducted raids at two separate locations within city limits, seizing more than 26kg of ganja in total.In Eloor, a West Bengal native was arrested with 14.13kg of ganja within Eloor police station limits. The accused, who worked collecting scrap for a shop in the Muttar area, was caught transporting the cannabis in his scrap-collecting three-wheeler at Manjummel. On Aug 31, a check conducted near Ernakulam South railway station within Kadavanthra police station limits led to the arrest of two Odisha natives with 12.15kg of cannabis in their possession.With more than 38kg of cannabis seized in less than a week, police have intensified their probe into the supply network bringing narcotics into the district from other states. Police have appealed to the public to report any information related to the smuggling and distribution of narcotics.
Article Summary: Charles Dennis, 29, and Praveen Das, 28, of Punnapra, Alappuzha, were arrested by a joint team of rural Dansaf unit and Angamaly Police. The ganja was found carefully packed in bags concealed in the car’s boot. Earlier this week, on Tuesday, Kochi city police conducted raids at two separate locations within city limits.
